Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can make the integration work smoothly with your existing stack:

Recap / technical areas discussed:
- SDK setup & auth: Node + Python SDKs available; options: API key (simple) or mTLS for stricter network controls.
- Routing / variants: per-route model pinning and policy-based routing (latency vs cost).
- Structured output & tool-calling: function-calling supported for deterministic JSON outputs and tool orchestration.
- Embeddings & rerankers: embeddings endpoint for vector generation and a reranker flow we recommend for relevance tuning.
- Observability hooks: headers and fields we suggest to correlate requests with your logs/dashboards.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you provision a dev sandbox domain and a list of IPs your infra will use? We can pre-authorize for mTLS if you prefer.
2) Please confirm which SDK (Node or Python) your engineers want to use so Mateo can drop an integration PR with example code.
3) Would you like a deep-dive with engineering on Monday (we have 9:30am or 2:00pm PT available)?

Observability guidance (high-level):
- Recommended trace header: X-Redwood-Trace-Id (we will accept X-Request-Id as fallback). Propagate this through your request chain.
- Latency breakdown header: X-Redwood-Latency — returned on responses with a pipe-separated breakdown: total|queue|compute (ms). Example: X-Redwood-Latency: 123|12|111
- Logging fields to capture on your side: request_id, user_id, model_version, batch_size, token_count, route_policy.
- Dashboards: we’ll provide a shared observability dashboard that surfaces per-route p95 latency, per-model error rate, and per-customer token consumption.

Attachments: demo recording + architecture diagram + SDK quickstart (links below).

I’ve looped in Mateo (SE) and Dev (developer advocate) — they’ll follow up with concrete snippets and a proposed runbook for authentication and headers.

Thanks — looking forward to the sandbox details.

Best,

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great questions — answering inline and adding concrete snippets below. I’ve attached the architecture diagram (arch-diagram-retailai.pdf) and the SDK quickstart we referenced.

mTLS / cert rotation:
- We support both approaches: (A) customer-managed mTLS certificates (you rotate certs on your schedule and we validate client certs), or (B) Redwood-managed certs with automated rotation via our platform (recommended for lower ops overhead).
- For AWS NLB/ALB termination: if you terminate at the LB, configure TCP pass-through to the Redwood private endpoint or use mutual TLS at the upstream. I’ll include example ALB listener rules in the attachment.

Latency breakdown / per-token timing:
- The response header X-Redwood-Latency provides an aggregate breakdown (total|queue|compute). We do not currently return per-token timing in headers due to bandwidth overhead on high-throughput flows.
- For per-token resolution we provide a streaming telemetry feed (Kafka or webhook) that emits token-level timestamps when enabled. You can subscribe to the stream for billing reconciliation. If you need this for all production traffic we can discuss sampling rate or an always-on plan (tradeoff = telemetry vs cost).

Embeddings batch endpoint / vector size:
- Use /v1/embeddings: supports batch payloads up to 512 inputs per request (payload-size dependent).
- Default vector dims depend on model; for our recommended open-model for similarity we return 768-dimensional vectors. For FAISS we recommend L2-normalized 768 vectors and using IVF+PQ for scale.

SDK snippet (Node) — minimal example to set headers and call structured output endpoint:

const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

(async () => {
  const res = await client.chat.create({
    model: 'redwood-chat-1',
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize order #1234' }],
    headers: {
      'X-Redwood-Trace-Id': 'retailai-req-0001',
      'X-Customer-Env': 'dev-retailai'
    },
    structured: true // enables deterministic JSON/function-calling output
  });
  console.log('response headers', res.headers['x-redwood-latency']);
})();

Logging fields we suggest capturing server-side:
- request_id (same as X-Redwood-Trace-Id)
- model_version
- route_policy
- batch_size
- token_count

Dashboards & observability handoff:
- I’ve provisioned a shared dashboard under the integration folder that shows per-route p50/p95, error rate, and per-model token costs. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-retailai-integration (we’ll add a direct Grafana link once we share read-only access).

Next steps / runbook (proposed):
- You: confirm preferred auth (mTLS vs API key) and provide test IPs by EOD Friday.
- Us: create sandbox creds + sample CI job that runs the Node quickstart against your IP allowlist.
- Schedule: engineering deep-dive Mon Jun 28 9:30am PT (we’ll send a calendar invite).

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the ALB snippets or the token telemetry options.

Cheers,
